title: Domain generalization for retinal vessel segmentation via Hessian-based vector field
mechanism: Represent thin vessels by the scaled minor eigenvector field of the Hessian, which is stable across imaging styles, plus a structure-preserving style augmentation.
adaptation: Bold bet for E1: add multi-scale dark-ridge Hessian eigenvector field channels (sigma 0.7 to 2.5 px) to the raw image; contrast invariance should help where 70% of E1 crack pixels get p < 0.001. Scuffs are also ridge-like but wider, so restrict sigma.
min_experiment: Arm: 3-channel [raw, vx, vy]; baseline house; 5 seeds; E1 crack recall and relF1@2; kill if E1 recall < +0.03. Run after the cheaper Frangi channel.
evidence: R (WebSearch summary, paper not read): train on fundus, test on OCT-A; extends MIDL 2022 Vector Field Transformer.

alt_notes.adaptation: Feed multi-scale Hessian orientation and eigenvalue channels to the house CNN (not their ViT) and add strong intensity-style augmentation; aimed at E1 (CSIR half-cut, scuff).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + Hessian channels + style aug, 5 seeds; baseline PF. Metric E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, test crack IoU guard. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03.
